bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in ihevcd_unpack_coeffs at decoder/ihevcd_iquant_itrans_recon_ctb.c:283. In the staged vulnerable source, residual parsing serializes each transform unit into the shared picture TU-coefficient buffer, and the multi-core process path later rebinds a worker cursor to that shared storage before ihevcd_iquant_itrans_recon_ctb calls ihevcd_unpack_coeffs for the crashing luma TU. ihevcd_unpack_coeffs rereads a positive coded-subblock count, a scan-header byte, and then u2_sig_coeff_map from the subblock record at the worker's current cursor. The loop is a do-while and never checks that the map is nonzero before WORD32 clz = CLZ(u4_sig_coeff_map); on x86 this helper returns 32 for CLZ(0), so sblk_scan_idx underflows from 31 to -1 and the next read gau1_ihevc_invscan4x4[u1_scan_type][sblk_scan_idx] lands one byte before the global 4x4 inverse-scan table, exactly matching the saved ASan report. The exact staged parser source separately proves that ihevcd_parse_residual_coding only writes subblock records after if(0 == num_coeff) continue, so parser-written u2_sig_coeff_map values are nonzero; the available static artifacts do not close which later shared-buffer or cursor state change made the crash-time reread zero. The staged patch is unrelated to this decoder path.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the current transform unit's shared coefficient-buffer state. Residual parsing reserves the TU header in pv_tu_coeff_data, initializes its count slot, serializes the scan/transform-skip byte, and advances the parse cursor to the first subblock record.
source.value_from: This statement is the earliest exact vulnerable-source point on the crashing path where attacker-shaped residual syntax is written into the shared picture TU-coefficient buffer that later crosses from parse context into process context. The reviewer-required reanchor is here, not at the later reconstruction-side reread.

tainted_value_origin.description: Earliest exact vulnerable-source write of an attacker-controlled TU header byte into the shared TU-coefficient buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: This scan/transform-skip byte is later reread at step 10 and contributes the inverse-scan row selector used at the sink. The crash-time zero u2_sig_coeff_map is a separate field whose source-level provenance remains unresolved.

root_cause.description: The unpack loop enters unconditionally as a do-while and never checks that u4_sig_coeff_map is nonzero before subtracting CLZ(u4_sig_coeff_map) from sblk_scan_idx.
root_cause.note: common/x86/ihevc_platform_macros.h defines CLZ(0) to return 32 on this build, so a zero crash-time map drives sblk_scan_idx from 31 to -1 before the inverse-scan lookup.

sink.description: ASan sink. With u1_scan_type resolved to row 0 and sblk_scan_idx underflowed to -1, this indexes one byte before global gau1_ihevc_invscan4x4.

parser_admitted.description: After NAL and slice-header parsing, this call admits the witness into slice-data parsing. The saved thread-creation stack also shows ihevcd_parse_pic_init -> ihevcd_parse_slice_data -> ihevcd_nal_unit on the crashing run.

evidence_limitations: run_flags.json sets runtime_disambiguation to false, and trace_feedback.json does not request runtime disambiguation, so Stage 02 must stay source-grounded and cannot add marker instrumentation to observe which upstream branch or cursor produced the zero reread.

The exact vulnerable parser source proves decoder/ihevcd_parse_residual.c:645 only serializes nonzero u2_sig_coeff_map values, while the saved ASan crash proves ihevcd_unpack_coeffs later consumes zero at decoder/ihevcd_iquant_itrans_recon_ctb.c:268. The available artifacts do not record the intermediate shared-buffer or cursor state change that connects those two facts.

The exact staged witness sets numCores = (data[7] % 4) + 1 = 4, so parse and process communicate through queued row jobs and the shared picture TU-coefficient buffer. That makes the handoff via i4_tu_coeff_data_ofst source-relevant, but the saved artifacts still do not reveal whether the crash-time zero came from a wrong row/TU cursor, stale or overwritten storage, or another upstream state transition.

The staged patch.diff only adds fuzzer/build files and does not touch decoder/ihevcd_parse_residual.c, decoder/ihevcd_parse_slice.c, decoder/ihevcd_process_slice.c, or decoder/ihevcd_iquant_itrans_recon_ctb.c, so it does not resolve or explain this crash path.

coarse_trace.summary: Because the exact witness selects four decoder cores, slice parsing queues a CMD_PROCESS job at CTB-row start and snapshots the current TU-coefficient cursor as i4_tu_coeff_data_ofst into the shared picture buffer.

Residual parsing materializes the current transform unit into the shared TU-coefficient buffer: it writes the TU header, serializes only subblock records with num_coeff != 0, advances the variable-length cursor, and backfills the final coded-subblock count.
When the queued job is dequeued, the worker rebinds ps_proc->pv_tu_coeff_data to pv_pic_tu_coeff_data + tu_coeff_data_ofst so reconstruction will read from the same picture-level TU buffer.

The crashing luma TU has b1_y_cbf == 1, so reconstruction rereads a positive coded-subblock count and a scan-header byte from the serialized TU buffer, reinterprets the remainder at the worker cursor as a subblock record, and loads u2_sig_coeff_map from that cursor.

That sink-side u2_sig_coeff_map reread is zero on the witness, but the staged artifacts do not show which earlier buffer or cursor transition produced it. The unchecked CLZ do-while underflows sblk_scan_idx to -1, and the inverse-scan table lookup reads one byte before gau1_ihevc_invscan4x4, matching ASan.

fine_trace.note: The exact staged witness sets numCores = (data[7] % 4) + 1 = 4, so slice parsing takes this multi-core branch at CTB-row start. It snapshots the current TU-coefficient cursor as an offset from the shared picture buffer base; the worker later uses this saved row-start offset to locate the shared region that the row's TU parser fills.

Source. For the current transform unit, residual parsing reserves the two-byte TU header in the shared picture TU-coefficient buffer, initializes the coded-subblock count slot, serializes the scan/transform-skip byte, and advances the parse cursor to the first subblock record.
This guard skips serialization for any 4x4 subblock whose significance map has no set bits. Only subblocks with at least one decoded coefficient reach the record write path below.

After step 3 passes, the parser counts this 4x4 block as coded and materializes its record at the current TU-coeff cursor. Because the zero-coefficient case already continued, the u2_sig_coeff_map written here is nonzero; this is source evidence about parser-written records, not a closed provenance edge to the sink-side zero reread.

The parse cursor advances past this subblock's fixed metadata and its num_coeff coefficient values. Later TUs and CTB rows are therefore addressed by the cumulative sizes of these variable-length records.

After all coded subblocks in the current transform unit are serialized, the parser backfills the header count that ihevcd_unpack_coeffs later rereads. The crashing path proves this final count is positive.

When the queued job is dequeued, the worker rebinds its TU-coeff cursor to the shared picture buffer base plus the row-start offset captured in step 1. ihevcd_utils.c seeds every process context with the same pv_pic_tu_coeff_data base, so parse and process now refer to the same picture-level storage.

On the crashing luma transform unit, b1_y_cbf is set, so reconstruction passes the rebound TU-coeff cursor into ihevcd_unpack_coeffs instead of leaving the block zeroed. The saved ASan stack names this exact call site at line 839.

ihevcd_unpack_coeffs first rereads the transform unit's coded-subblock count from the serialized header. Because the loop body reaches the crash, this count is positive on the witnessed path and is consistent with the backfill at step 6.

Next it rereads the scan-header byte written at step 2, extracts the low trans_skip bit, and keeps the inverse-scan row selector in u1_scan_type. The saved fault address one byte before gau1_ihevc_invscan4x4 is consistent with row 0 on the crashing path.

After the two-byte TU header is consumed, the remaining buffer at the worker's current cursor is reinterpreted as a 4x4 subblock record. The staged artifacts do not establish whether this cursor still names the exact parser-written record that step 4 populated.

Crash-time read of the u2_sig_coeff_map field from the subblock record at the current worker cursor. Step 4 proves parser-written records carry nonzero maps, yet the later underflow and ASan address require this reread to be 0; the available artifacts do not close which intervening shared-buffer or cursor state change produced that zero.

Root cause. The loop is a do-while, so it executes once even when the map is zero, and there is no guard before CLZ(u4_sig_coeff_map). On x86, CLZ(0) returns 32, so the crash-time zero from step 12 underflows sblk_scan_idx from 31 to -1 before the table lookup.

ASan sink. With u1_scan_type resolved from step 10 and sblk_scan_idx underflowed to -1 in step 13, this read lands one byte before global gau1_ihevc_invscan4x4 at common/ihevc_common_tables.c:271, exactly matching the saved global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.

format.contract: The exact staged poc file for OSS-Fuzz testcase 5101556982087680. The verified trigger semantics are limited to this witness: Stage 01 reproduced a run that reaches ihevcd_unpack_coeffs with a positive coded-subblock count, a scan-header byte that selects inverse-scan row 0 at the sink, and a crash-time reread of u2_sig_coeff_map == 0 from the subblock record at the worker's current cursor; that zero drives CLZ(0), underflows sblk_scan_idx, and produces the saved global-buffer-overflow read. This contract does not claim that ihevcd_parse_residual.c serialized a zero map or that neighboring HEVC inputs follow the same path.
